pillar_reactions.evidence: Asked 'any questions on that?' he answered 'Nope.' He arrived pre-sold — found Trevor on TikTok about a year ago, had physical therapy put him on goblet squats and kettlebell deadlifts, and reported 'I liked working with the kettlebell. I liked being able to kind of do things a little more isometric to make sure that I'm working on balance on both sides instead of compensating with one side.' The one thing he specifically wanted from the pillar was safety — 'I would just love to do more of it and have that coaching to make sure I'm doing it correctly so I don't get hurt.'

'Nope' to questions. The eight-hour-window framing collided directly with his military-conditioned schedule of eating from about 7am and being full by 5pm, and he engaged with that honestly rather than resisting it — 'It's been like that because in the military, your dinner time will start at like four, but you're usually eating breakfast around five or six.' He accepted that it would need adjusting and the rep deferred the specifics to Trevor. He also independently articulated the sustainability principle before the rep did: 'if I started getting too nitty gritty... it's not sustainable. I want to enjoy my food more than I want to look good.'

The pillar that sold him, and he said why in his own words: 'the accountability piece is huge. I don't have anybody to share my success with or bounce ideas off of or be like, hey, how can I adjust this? So that'll be huge.' He also volunteered that the weekly check-in matched his existing habit — 'That's about how often I'm weighing in and checking in on myself. So once a week is perfect' — and pre-solved the travel objection himself: 'most of the places we go, we drive, and I can throw a kettlebell in a car.' Even the video submission, which two other prospects in this batch flinched at, he resolved instantly: 'That's fine. It's just Trevor... That's like just sending it to a friend.'

anchors.raw: I only recently went and suspended my gym membership because I was like, I'm not going to pay to come here anymore. I'm not having a good time, besties.
anchors.note: His most recent decision about paying for fitness was to stop paying for fitness, and the amount in his head is a monthly gym fee. He is also mid-deleveraging — 'we've been paying off a lot of stuff' — with a 580s credit score and a new half-million-dollar mortgage. The rep never surfaced or reframed this; he went straight to financing mechanics.

anchors.raw: there was a, on the site when I booked, when I watched the video, there was like a printout of like a beginner thing. I might mess around with those this weekend a little bit.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's TikTok and the free beginner printout
anchors.note: Third prospect in this batch already using the free version of the product, and here he planned to start using it over the weekend regardless of whether he bought. He had also already purchased an adjustable kettlebell off his own back. The self-serve path was open and he was walking down it while the decision waited on his wife.

anchors.raw: she's definitely seeing, and she's been unhappy with her body, too, and she's got her own thing going on... She's been like, I need you to make sure I'm getting up and I'm doing stuff.
anchors.note: The single most valuable unused asset on this call. The wife is the gatekeeper on the purchase and is simultaneously dissatisfied with her own fitness, asking him to help her get moving, and already familiar with Trevor's videos. That is the answer to 'is there any reason she would NOT want you doing this', and it was volunteered ten minutes before the spouse objection landed. It was never brought back.

anchors.raw: Yeah, I've used Klarna a ton. I've used Affirm a ton.
anchors.note: Instalment purchasing is normal behaviour for him, which is why the Payva route worked and was approved despite a 580s score. Offset by the fact that third-party financing added roughly $1,800 to the cost, and no company-side plan was offered as a cheaper alternative.

unmet_demand.want: Programming built around an unresolved spine fracture with surgery anticipated, coordinated with the clinicians already treating him
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asked one genuinely good screening question about squats and then closed the topic with 'we need to work around that' and a promise that Trevor would get into detail. Nobody asked what the treating physician or physical therapist has cleared, whether the anticipated surgery has a date, what happens to a six-month programme if he goes under the knife in month three, or whether Trevor will speak to a clinician. The prospect's own stated reason for wanting coaching is 'to make sure I'm doing it correctly so I don't get hurt', and that is exactly the assurance that was not given.

unmet_demand.want: A way to bring his wife in alongside him — 'then I can teach her, you know what I mean? Maybe when she gets a little more ready... even if it's something she only does for 20 minutes'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No partner, household or second-seat option exists in the offer and none was described. The rep answered with a story about a different client leading by example rather than with anything purchasable. This is the second time in the batch a prospect has raised a partner wanting in — Tyler Stillwater's wife on 2026-07-07 — and both times it was left as an anecdote. Here it is doubly costly because the partner is also the person whose approval is blocking the sale.

unmet_demand.want: To fund the programme from a Health Savings Account, or reimburse himself from one
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Payva declined the HSA card and the prospect emailed his HR to ask about self-reimbursement, making the answer a dependency on the sale. Nobody established whether a fitness coaching programme is an eligible expense, and the rep encouraged the route rather than clarifying it. Whether the product can or should be represented as a qualifying medical expense is unresolved and material.
